data.name: labs.automationextensions.recordresult.explanation
data.value: Saves whether this step succeeded, so a later "Previous step succeeded" condition can branch on it.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.resultsource.explanation
data.value: Type of the earlier step whose result is checked. The step must have "Record result for later steps" turned on.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.resultnumber.write.explanation
data.value: Select the same step and number in the "Previous step succeeded" condition. When a process has several steps of this type, give each one a different number.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.resultnumber.read.explanation
data.value: Number selected on the earlier step. If no earlier step saved this result, contacts follow the No branch.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.skipstep.action.explanation
data.value: Contacts move on without this step running. Use when you can't delete the step because the process already has contact history. Tip: start the step name with "[Skipped]" (or ⏭️) so it's visible in the builder.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.skipstep.condition.explanation
data.value: The condition isn't checked and all contacts follow the branch selected below. This applies only when the component is enabled by your administrator. If disabled by application configuration, all library conditions follow No (A), regardless of this setting. Use when you can't delete the step because the process already has contact history. Tip: start the step name with "[Skipped → Yes]" or "[Skipped → No]" so it's visible in the builder. If you turn skipping off later, make sure both branches lead to further steps.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.skippedbranch.explanation
data.value: Branch all contacts follow while the step is skipped.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.description
data.value: Sends the contact to an external system (CRM, CDP, Zapier, Power Automate). Endpoints are set up by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.endpoint.explanation
data.value: System that receives the contact. Missing a destination? Ask your developers to add it to the application configuration.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.eventname.explanation
data.value: Tells the receiving system what happened, for example "lead-qualified" or "webinar-registered".

data.name: labs.automationextensions.sendwebhook.includecontactdetails.explanation
data.value: Adds email, first name, last name, and company name. Leave off to send only an anonymous contact ID. Only enable when the destination is allowed to receive personal data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.description
data.value: Writes a message to the Event log for every contact reaching this step. Use to check which path contacts take. Usually enabled only during testing.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.message.explanation
data.value: Text written to the log. You can use {processName}, {contactId}, {contactGuid}, and {triggerIdentifier}. Don't include personal data.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.level.explanation
data.value: Use Warning or Error for paths that need attention, for example when a webhook failed.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.includestepresults.explanation
data.value: Adds results saved by earlier steps, for example whether "Send webhook" succeeded. Helps explain why a "Previous step succeeded" condition took a branch.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.writetolog.includetriggerdetails.explanation
data.value: Adds what started the process, for example the submitted form or the contact date.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.previousstepsucceeded.description
data.value: Checks whether an earlier step (for example "Send webhook") succeeded. Use after a step with "Record result for later steps" turned on.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.description
data.value: Assigns each contact to a stable Yes (A) or No (B) branch. Requires administrator enablement; when disabled by application configuration, all contacts follow No (A), regardless of skip settings.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.percentage.explanation
data.value: When enabled by your administrator, this percentage (0–100) of contacts follows Yes (A); the rest follow No (B). Allocation is approximate, not an exact count. When disabled by application configuration, all contacts follow No (A), regardless of this percentage or skip settings. Ask your administrator to confirm whether this component is enabled.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.splitkey.explanation
data.value: Stable name for this split, default "default". Same contact and key always get the same bucket, even after a process is renamed. Keys are case-sensitive; spaces matter.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.randomsplit.splitkey.required
data.value: Enter a split key containing at least one non-space character.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactdateanniversary.description
data.value: Starts once a year on (or before) a contact date, such as a birthday. Runs daily – requires a scheduled task set up by your developers.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactdateanniversary.datefield.explanation
data.value: Only the month and day are used, so the process starts every year. Missing a field? Ask your developers to add it to the application configuration.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.contactdateanniversary.daysbefore.explanation
data.value: Start on the date or a number of days before it. Set the process recurrence to "If not already running" ("Only once" would start it only in the first year).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.description
data.value: Checks if the current time (when this condition runs) falls within a configured time window. This is NOT a Wait step – time is evaluated immediately.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.starttime.explanation
data.value: Window opens at this time, inclusive (e.g., 14:00 matches 14:00:00). For overnight windows (e.g., 22:00–02:00), the selected weekday refers to the day the window starts.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.endtime.explanation
data.value: Window closes at this time, exclusive (e.g., 16:00 matches up to 15:59:59). Can be earlier than start time for overnight windows (e.g., 22:00–02:00).

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.timezone.explanation
data.value: The host's local time zone. UTC is the default. The time zone ID is saved and must exist on any deployment host. Zones not available on deployment hosts cause an error – contact your administrator.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.startdate.explanation
data.value: Limits the time window to dates on or after this date, inclusive. Leave blank for no limit.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.withintimewindow.enddate.explanation
data.value: Limits the time window to dates on or before this date, inclusive. Leave blank for no limit. Must be on or after the start date.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.stepregistry.scope.content
data.value:
This tab lists the registered trigger, action, and condition definitions for the whole application, not just this process. It does not inspect which steps this process uses.

Status shows the effective state of library components; the default is disabled unless application configuration enables them.

data.name: labs.automationextensions.stepregistry.disabled.content
data.value:
When a library condition is disabled, all contacts follow the "No" path without evaluating the condition. Administrator disablement overrides marketer skip settings.
Disabled library actions do nothing (contacts continue); disabled library triggers cannot start processes. All disabled steps log warnings in the Event Log when run.
